counterfactual_missing_items: which had resolved prior to surgery
no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, and no epithelial defect
The anterior chamber was deep and clear
decisive_items: history of an eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa (pine processionary) 9 months before DSAEK
brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma
response.rationale: R4 is the only candidate with a specific causal anchor: prior Thaumetopoea pityocampa exposure plus deep brown multilobular corneal lesions. Prior clinical resolution does not exclude retained setae or a delayed immune reaction triggered by DSAEK and corticosteroids. R2 is the main structural differential because of deep stromal infiltrates, but it lacks a causal link and is weakened by intact epithelium, no discharge, and a clear anterior chamber. R1 and R5 are nonspecific mechanism/context labels without independent confirming spans.

rejected.why: Immune-mediated keratitis is a mechanism rather than the specific diagnosis; no graft rejection line, anterior chamber reaction, or other immune rejection marker is described.
Corticosteroid use is only a risk factor or treatment context; it does not explain brown multilobular deep stromal lesions or the prior Thaumetopoea pityocampa exposure.
